ai_claim.claim: Unilever describes AI-supported supply-chain planning in production, but the retrieved public material did not provide a controlled waste/service/cash cohort.
ai_claim.stage: E1 supply-chain capability; no opened controlled cohort
ai_claim.scope: Specific workflow only; infrastructure demand is separated from own productivity.
ai_claim.limitation: No representative controlled cohort or retained-cash reconciliation.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: commodity/input inflation and pricing response dominate margins.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Does not itself disprove the scoped mechanism.

rights_limit: Public terms do not prove universal training or pooled cross-customer reuse; enterprise schedules were unavailable.
materiality_summary: Framework convention: €520m, 5% of a €10.4bn annualized H1 underlying operating-profit proxy. Illustrative assumptions produce €90m, below the hurdle.

arithmetic.inputs: pool €12bn eligible supply-chain, marketing-production and support cost; efficiency 10%; realization 40%; retained share 50%; recurring cost €150m
arithmetic.formula: eligible cost × efficiency × realization × retained share − recurring AI expense
